_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.
generatedBy: weekly scout, 2026-09-21 — the week the speech lane got measured and the two boxes diverged. B5 took Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3-TTS into service on 20-09; BeTenshi took Chatterbox on 18-09 and left its STT on whisper-large-v3, which is open #36 of 52 on the Open ASR Leaderboard. The Open TTS Leaderboard (build 18-09-2026) now measures the models this report has been ranking on adoption, and it contradicts three things earlier runs asserted: Kokoro is not the weak link, Qwen3-TTS does not beat it on English, and the VibeVoice WER this report quoted for two weeks belongs to a different checkpoint.

candidates.name: Cohere Transcribe (03-2026)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 21-09 and byte-for-byte unchanged: model.safetensors 4,131,862,976 B plus config and tokenizer = 4,134,794,009 B for the whole repo. Against the 2,065,804,048 params HF reports that is exactly 2 bytes/param, so it is a plain bf16 release with no codec or encoder outside the count. VRAM is 4.13 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only. Benchmarks are from the Open ASR Leaderboard build dated 19-09-2026 — english_short_latest.csv at rev 7e57dda, longform_latest.csv at rev 13d1000, multilingual_*.csv at the revs listed in the Space's init.py — not from this box.

candidates.why: THE PICK FOR BETENSHI, and the one thing on this list most worth doing this week. BeTenshi still serves stt from whisper-large-v3 on :8001, which on the 19-09 board sits at 5.78 average WER — open #36 of 52 on short-form English. Cohere is still the only open model that beats it on ALL THREE boards rather than trading one for another: short-form English 4.67 vs 5.78, long-form 9.73 vs 11.23 (top open model outright), multilingual 3.84 vs 4.57 (also top open). 906 RTFx against whisper's 470, for a 4.13 GB download. Its 14 declared languages include ARABIC, which no other candidate here covers and which this box has an evaluation harness for (config/arabic-eval.json, docs/arabic-model-experiment-2026-09-14.md). Nothing about it changed this week — the numbers, the byte counts and the 4.13 GB are identical to last week's read — which is the point: it was the pick seven days ago and it was not taken, while B5 moved its own STT off whisper on 20-09 and BeTenshi did not. The two boxes now disagree about how well this house transcribes audio, and BeTenshi is the one that lost. Unremarkable on B5, which has the pool for it and a better incumbent already. The one caveat is unchanged: the repo is `gated: auto`, a click-through rather than an application, so a human clicks it and reads the terms first. apache-2.0, 207K downloads in the last 30 days and 3.36M all-time.

candidates.name: AuK-Flash (Tencent Hunyuan speech foundation model, distilled)
candidates.params: the Open TTS Leaderboard records 1.53B; HF publishes no count and the repo ships 6.76 GB, so the count is still not the footprint

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, read 21-09: auk_flash.safetensors 6,122,209,092 B + vae.safetensors 637,322,604 B = 6,759,531,696 B of weights, 6,762,657,045 B for the whole repo. Byte-for-byte the same size as the AuK base repo, which ships the same VAE beside auk_base.safetensors at the identical 6,122,209,092 B. HF publishes NO parameter count for either repo — the safetensors index carries no dtype summary — so estimateFromParams() must not be used on them; the leaderboard's 1.53B against 6.76 GB of weights would be 4.4 bytes/param, so that figure describes one component and not the checkpoint. VRAM is 6.76 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured. Host RAM is the server process only: at 6.76 GB the weight set fits on BeTenshi's card outright, so unlike the image models it needs no CPU offload and holds no standing host-RAM cost. Benchmarks are the Open TTS Leaderboard build dated 18-09-2026 (hf-audio/tts_leaderboard_results at rev 4b9b89c, read through the Space's own API because the results dataset is not publicly downloadable).

candidates.why: CORRECTING LAST WEEK IN THE OPEN, twice. This entry was `tencent/AuK` and it was argued on the claim that nothing on this box could clone a voice. That claim died on 18 September, when Chatterbox shipped as the `voice` service on :8004 — so the old reason is gone. What replaces it is better, because the Open TTS Leaderboard now measures both. On the one dataset and language where the running service and this model are both scored — CV3-Eval, English, voice-cloning mode — AuK-Flash gets 72.67 speaker similarity against Chatterbox-multilingual's 53.13, 3.35 WER against 4.43, and 26.61 RTFx against 0.99. That is +19.5 SIM points on the one axis a cloning service exists for, lower error, and roughly 27x the throughput, under the same MIT licence. On Seed-TTS English the gap is the same shape: AuK-Flash 0.80 WER / 75.71 SIM against ChatterboxTTS 1.07 / 59.51. The second correction is the checkpoint: this was carried as the AuK base model and the board says take Flash instead — the two are the same 6.76 GB and Flash trades 0.11 WER for 4-6x the speed (26.61 vs 4.28 RTFx on CV3, 18.55 vs 4.47 on Seed-TTS), which is the whole difference between a service and a batch job. THE COST, stated plainly: AuK-Flash declares zh and en only, where Chatterbox declares 23 languages including Arabic, and neither board measures Arabic at all. Chatterbox in cloning mode ranks 7th across all nine CV3 languages at 66.40 SIM, so it is not bad at breadth — it is far behind on English quality and slower than real time. So this is a second cloning voice for English and Chinese, not a replacement for what is running, and it is a new service to write rather than a repoint of :8004: AuK is an instruction-driven pipeline that also does speech editing, enhancement and source separation, which nothing on either box can do. On BeTenshi 6.76 GB sits on the card beside Kokoro and Chatterbox without disturbing them; unremarkable on B5.

candidates.name: Qwen3-TTS 12Hz (1.7B CustomVoice)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 21-09 and unchanged: model.safetensors 3,833,402,552 B (= 1,916,676,352 params x 2 bytes, so bf16) PLUS speech_tokenizer/model.safetensors 682,293,092 B, which the 1.7B in the name does not include — 4,520,218,951 B for the whole repo. VRAM is that x 1.15 runtime overhead. Not measured. Ignore the repo's `usedStorage` of 4,604,822,661 B; it counts revisions the download does not fetch.

candidates.why: ADOPTED ON B5 on 20-09 — config/hosts/b5.json now serves `qwen3-tts-1.7b-customvoice` through the LocalAI adapter — so this entry speaks only to BETENSHI from here on, and its case there has been rewritten from the ground up because the Open TTS Leaderboard contradicted the old one. THE OLD ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN: this entry said 'local-kokoro is 82M and sounds like it' and offered this as the upgrade. On the board, Kokoro-82M scores 1.46 average WER on English at 69.0 RTFx — second of 29 models, ahead of this one's 1.71 at 13.32 RTFx, with a 103.9 ms time-to-first-audio against this one's 309.9 ms. For reading English aloud the 82M model already installed is faster, more intelligible and a fortieth of the size, and nothing should repoint :8002. WHAT SURVIVES IS BREADTH, and it is a real gap on BeTenshi. Across all nine languages CV3-Eval measures, this model ranks 3rd at 4.22 average WER; Kokoro is unranked because it has no German, Korean or Russian at all, and the multilingual voice this box actually gained on 18-09 — Chatterbox — ranks 10th at 11.28. Per language, reading without cloning: German 5.96 against Chatterbox's 17.45, French 5.94 against 16.34, Russian 5.70 against 13.49, Japanese 5.90 against 8.82. So if BeTenshi needs to read non-English text aloud, this is the model, it beats what shipped three days ago by two to three times on error, and B5 has already made that call for itself. One factual correction to the old entry while we are here: the board records CustomVoice as NOT supporting voice cloning — the `-Base` sibling is the cloning variant, and it is the one ranked 3rd in cloning mode at 72.60 SIM. 'CustomVoice' is a speaker bank, not zero-shot cloning. Downloads, stated by metric as docs/models.md requires: 2.57M in the last 30 days, 15.17M all-time. The old 'most-pulled clean-licensed TTS on the hub by an order of magnitude' is withdrawn and was never supportable — Chatterbox leads it 22.0M to 15.2M on lifetime and trails 1.83M to 2.57M on the month, and neither gap is remotely 10x.

candidates.name: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (transformers build)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 21-09 and byte-for-byte unchanged: model.safetensors 4,076,193,080 B plus tokenizer and config = 4,087,646,324 B for the whole repo. That file size divided by the 2,038,052,480 params HF reports is exactly 2 bytes/param, so the release is bf16 and there is no hidden encoder or codec outside the count. VRAM is 4.09 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only. B5 runs an 8-bit MLX build instead, which is roughly half this on disk — that figure has not been read off B5 and is not claimed here.

candidates.why: ADOPTED ON B5 on 20-09 — config/hosts/b5.json serves `qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit` through MLX-Audio — so this entry now speaks only to BETENSHI, where :8001 is still whisper-large-v3. It keeps its place there for one narrow reason and loses on everything else. It is open #1 on the Open ASR Leaderboard's short-form English board — 4.31% average WER against whisper's 5.78%, a 25% relative error reduction, at 820 RTFx against 470 — and tenth overall, with every model above it proprietary. On the multilingual board it averages 5.53% against whisper's 4.57%: WORSE than the model it would replace on every one of the six measured European languages except German and Spanish, despite the 30 languages its metadata advertises. It is absent from the long-form board entirely, so nothing is known about how it handles a meeting recording rather than a clean utterance. Cohere above beats it on two boards of three and loses the third by 0.36 points, which is why Cohere is the pick and this is the specialist: take it on BeTenshi only if that box transcribes short English audio and nothing else, which is what voice input in the Studio actually is. The fact that it has now been in service on B5 for a day is evidence it runs, not evidence it is right for the other box.

candidates.name: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming 1.5B
candidates.params: 2.81B (the '1.5B' in the name is the LLM backbone only)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 21-09 and unchanged: model-0000{1,2,3}-of-00003.safetensors 2,498,354,152 + 2,486,576,066 + 643,458,072 B = 5.63 GB of weights, 5,645,212,528 B for the whole repo. Against the 2,814,116,321 params HF reports that is exactly 2 bytes/param, so it is a bf16 release with no separate codec outside the count. Note the name understates it: '1.5B' is the language backbone, the checkpoint is 2.81B. VRAM is 5.63 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only.

candidates.why: CORRECTING LAST WEEK IN THE OPEN: this entry quoted '5.58% short-form English' and '11.90% multilingual' as this model's scores, and they are not. Those rows belong to `microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF`, a DIFFERENT checkpoint — 8B, 50 declared languages — which is what the Open ASR Leaderboard actually measures. Re-read at the 19-09 build and confirmed identical in the 11-09 build this report was reading at the time, so the mistake was mine and not the board's: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-1.5B is ABSENT FROM ALL THREE BOARDS and its accuracy is unmeasured, full stop. Every accuracy claim made about it here for the last two weeks should be struck. What is left is what was always the real case, and it needs no benchmark: it is the only MIT-licensed model on this list that streams speaker-attributed transcription as audio arrives, and local-whisper on BeTenshi cannot show live text or tell two speakers apart at all. So install it for live diarised transcription, behind its own service, and do not repoint the stt capability at it — the general route belongs to Cohere. If diarisation alone is the need, OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize IS measured: 4.64% short-form English in 0.91 GB under Apache-2.0, against a multilingual 9.08, so English-first, and the better buy on every axis except the streaming itself. On BeTenshi 5.65 GB sits comfortably beside the speech services; the 7B sibling at 17.36 GB runs alone there and blocks every image model, and is unremarkable on B5 — that is where the 7B goes if its accuracy is wanted.

upgrades.why: Raised 2026-09-07, so TWO WEEKS outstanding, read from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json` rather than counted by hand. The price case is re-verified this week against OpenAI's published pricing page and holds exactly: gpt-5.5 is $5.00/$30.00 per 1M input/output tokens, gpt-5.6-terra is $2.00/$12.00 — a 2.5x cut on both sides of the meter for a model OpenAI positions as performance-competitive. BUT ONE CLAIM THIS ENTRY MADE IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN: it said gpt-5.5 'is no longer carried in OpenAI's published pricing table'. It is still carried, alongside gpt-5.5-pro at $30/$180. The urgency is therefore cost, not retirement — which is a weaker argument than the one made last week, and the entry should not have implied a deadline it could not support. Terra, not sol ($4/$20) or luna ($0.20/$1.20): sol is the flagship and luna the cheap tier, so both change what the alias means, and this alias is the stable one applications call. This is exactly the repoint docs/models.md says the console cannot make for you — familyKey() strips version tokens and cannot see that 'terra' is a tier name, so gpt-5.5 -> gpt-5.6-terra never gets the `supersedes` label. All three 5.6 ids are already wired under their own names from the 2026-08-19 wire-all; only the alias is stale.

Unchanged, and now THIRTY-THREE DAYS outstanding — first raised 2026-08-19, read from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json`, not incremented from last week's 'four weeks'. claude-opus-5 shipped 2026-07-24 and claude-opus-4-8 on 2026-05-28: two generations on, same tier, same alias. The wire-all on 2026-08-19 added a separate `claude-opus-5` alias, so the model is already reachable and already paid for; the stable hand-written `claude-opus` alias that applications call is the only thing still pointing at 4-8. A one-line edit to ai-router.yaml that nothing in the console will do for you.

notes: ADOPTED SINCE THE LAST RUN, and the reason three entries above were rewritten rather than repeated. BETENSHI took ResembleAI/chatterbox into service on 18-09 as the `voice` service on :8004 — it is in config/model-meta.json as local-chatterbox and in ai-router.yaml as an audio_speech alias, kept deliberately below Kokoro so defaultServiceFor() still falls back to the 82M model. THE TTS RANKING, from the Open TTS Leaderboard build dated 18-09-2026 — the first time this report has ranked text-to-speech on a benchmark rather than on downloads, and it overturns more than it confirms. The board scores intelligibility (WER of a Qwen3-ASR transcription of the generated speech), throughput (RTFx) and, in cloning mode only, speaker similarity (SIM against a WavLM embedding of the reference clip). It does NOT score naturalness or prosody, so nothing here says which model sounds nicer — only which one says the words and which one sounds like the person it was asked to sound like. ENGLISH, no cloning, averaged over Seed-TTS and CV3-Eval, WER lower better: VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B 1.44, hexgrad/Kokoro-82M 1.46 at 69.0 RTFx, Supertone/supertonic-3 1.54, fishaudio/s2-pro 1.58, k2-fsa/OmniVoice 1.61, kyutai/pocket-tts 1.62, ResembleAI/chatterbox 1.70, Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice 1.71 at 13.3 RTFx, Breeze-TTS-2 1.72, tencent/AuK 2.48, AuK-Flash 2.70, VoxCPM2 3.38. ENGLISH, cloning, CV3-Eval, WER / SIM: AuK 3.24 / 73.00, AuK-Flash 3.35 / 72.67, Chatterbox-multilingual 4.43 / 53.13. ALL NINE LANGUAGES, CV3-Eval, no cloning: OmniVoice 3.39, Qwen3-TTS-CustomVoice 4.22 (rank 3), VoxCPM2 4.45, Chatterbox-multilingual 11.28 (rank 10); Kokoro, AuK and AuK-Flash are unranked because they do not cover all nine. STREAMING, time-to-first-audio at batch 1 on an H200: Kokoro 103.9 ms, Qwen3-TTS-CustomVoice 309.9 ms. Three corrections fall out, and all three are this report's own. Kokoro is not the weak link — it is second on English and the fastest thing near the top, and 'sounds like it' was a guess dressed as a finding. Qwen3-TTS does not beat it on English and never did; its case is breadth. And AuK, which this report recommended on its licence and its capability list, turns out to be measurably the best zero-shot cloner on the board by speaker similarity, which is a better reason than the one given.

THE STT RANKING, from the Open ASR Leaderboard build dated 19-09-2026 (english_short_latest.csv rev 7e57dda, longform_latest.csv rev 13d1000, multilingual_*.csv at the revisions in the Space's init.py). Open-weights models by average WER, lower better, against local-whisper (openai/whisper-large-v3) as BeTenshi's incumbent. SHORT-FORM ENGLISH: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 4.31 (open #1, 10th overall — every model above it is proprietary), Hojo-ASR-V1 4.33, higgs-audio-v3-stt 4.39, canary-qwen-2.5b 4.43, ARK-ASR-3B 4.48, ARK-ASR-0.6B 4.56, granite-speech-4.1-2b 4.62, MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 4.64, Cohere Transcribe 4.67, granite-speech-4.1-2b-nar 4.68, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 4.70, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 4.86, VibeVoice-ASR-HF 5.58, whisper-large-v3 5.78 (open #36 of 52), whisper-large-v3-turbo 6.36, nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming 7.88 (open #46). LONG-FORM: Cohere 9.73 (open #1), parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 10.72, whisper-turbo 11.01, whisper-large-v3 11.23 — Qwen3-ASR, the VibeVoice models, MOSS, ARK-ASR and the granite 4.1 pair are NOT MEASURED here at all. MULTILINGUAL, mean of FLEURS/MCV/MLS across fr-de-es-it-pt-nl: Cohere 3.84 (open #1), whisper-large-v3 4.57, parakeet 5.25, Qwen3-ASR 5.53, MOSS 9.08, VibeVoice-ASR-HF 11.90; ARK-ASR is absent and granite-4.1-2b-nar has only four of the six. The board did not move for the models this report already tracked — Qwen3-ASR, Cohere and whisper are unchanged to three decimals from the 11-09 build. What moved is this report's reading of it, twice over. See the VibeVoice entry above for the misattribution; the second miss is that ARK-ASR-0.6B/3B and the granite-speech-4.1 pair were ALREADY on the 11-09 board when this report claimed to have ranked it, and were not mentioned. Both are recorded below rather than promoted, because Cohere still beats them where it matters.

STT models seen and NOT picked, with their numbers, so the next run does not re-litigate them. Edge0/ARK-ASR-0.6B (the board still calls it AutoArk-AI; the repo redirects to Edge0) is the miss worth naming: apache-2.0, 1.30B params, 2.62 GB, 19 European and Asian languages, 4.56 short-form English at 663 RTFx — better than Cohere on that one board and 1.5 GB smaller — but absent from long-form and multilingual entirely, and with 7,233 all-time downloads it is unproven anywhere. ARK-ASR-3B is 4.48 for 4.06B params. ibm-granite/granite-speech-4.1-2b is 4.62 at 545 RTFx with 2.0M downloads, and its -nar sibling is 4.68 at 2,074 RTFx — 4.4x whisper's throughput under apache-2.0, which makes it the fast-and-accurate option if latency ever becomes the constraint; both are en/fr/de/es/pt only and neither is on the long-form board. nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 remains the speed outlier at 6,076 RTFx, 0.6 GB, 26 languages, cc-by-4.0, and respectable everywhere (4.86 / 10.72 / 5.25); it stays out only because nothing on either box is throughput-bound today. OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize is the better diarisation model than VibeVoice on every measured axis — 4.64 short-form, 0.91 GB, Apache-2.0, 50 declared languages — but its multilingual average is 9.08, so treat it as English diarisation. mistralai/Voxtral-Small-24B-2507 is the best open multilingual model after Cohere (3.74) and is 24B: won't fit BeTenshi, comfortable on B5. bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-stt (4.39) and HojoAI/Hojo-ASR-V1 (4.33) score well but declare 1 and 2 languages. Held out on licence: netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 is the #1 trending ASR model this week and is `license:other` — its parameter count is 2,038,052,480, byte-identical to Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-hf, so it is a fine-tune of a model already on this list and the licence is the only thing it adds; oruk/orukeet is unchanged at cc-by-sa-4.0 (25 European languages, a 714 MB q8 GGUF that would be the first ASR upgrade here costing LESS than the incumbent, still waiting on a human to read the share-alike terms); nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b remains `license:other`; Quran-Lab/zipformer_p-arabic-v3 is an Arabic specialist that would be interesting given config/arabic-eval.json, but it is gated AND `other` and publishes no benchmark.

TTS ALTERNATIVES seen and not adopted, now with numbers instead of download counts. openbmb/VoxCPM2 was held out for a month as 'the standing near-miss, 0.44 GB larger than Qwen3-TTS for the same job'. It is not the same job and that framing is withdrawn: it is mediocre at plain reading (3.38 English WER, and 1.75-1.79 RTFx, which is the second-slowest thing on the board) and strong at cloning (1.82 WER / 70.87 SIM on English, rank 5 across all nine languages at 74.69 SIM), under apache-2.0 with 30 declared languages and 4.96 GB on disk. If multilingual CLONING is ever the need, it and not AuK is the apache-2.0 answer, because AuK covers two languages. k2-fsa/OmniVoice is the best open TTS model measured — #1 on both nine-language boards, 0.81B, 8.6M all-time downloads — and stays out on licence: the repo publishes NO licence tag at all, and the leaderboard records cc-by-nc, which is a third-party claim and non-commercial either way. Held out on licence, unchanged: BreezeBlue/Breeze-TTS-2 (3.47B, `other`, and now measurably behind — 1.72 English WER, and its trending score halved from 194-era AuK's rise), bosonai/higgs-tts-3-4b (`other`, 102 declared languages, 3.23 English WER, still the widest coverage in open TTS and still the reason to read that licence if coverage is the constraint), fishaudio/s2-pro (`other`, 1.58 WER but 0.4 RTFx — slower than every other model on the board), IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5 and Supertone/supertonic-3 (Open RAIL-M, 1.54 WER at 47 RTFx, 31 languages — the one on this list most worth a licence read). microsoft/VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B tops the English no-cloning board at 1.44 under MIT and covers 10 languages, but it collapses outside English (German 20.72, Japanese 21.97, Korean 26.24) and is unranked; on English alone it is a 1.36B model to beat Kokoro's 82M by 0.02 WER, which is not a reason to download anything.

THE IMAGE LANE IS STILL EMPTY, and this week's #1 trending text-to-image model is why it stays that way. Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 landed on 14-09 with 938 likes and the top trending score on the hub, and it is `license:other` — unread terms, so it waits in this note per docs/models.md regardless of merit. It is also the week's best illustration of the footprint pattern: HF reports 7,115,124,736 params, which at bf16 would be 14.2 GB, and the repo ships 33.13 GB because the text encoder alone is 17.5 GB across four shards. That is over BeTenshi's 31.8 GB card before the transformer is even counted, and unremarkable in B5's 128 GB pool — but the licence decides it on both boxes, not the size. krea/Krea-2-Turbo and Krea-2-Raw remain gated AND `other` at 12.82B/62.0 GB. FLUX.1-dev is `other`; the rest of the trending list is Krea LoRAs and GGUF repacks of the two. Nothing in text-to-image this week is both clean-licensed and better than the Z-Image-Turbo / FLUX.2-klein-4B / HiDream-O1 trio installed and measured on 12 September.

TWO MACHINES, and this is the week the difference stopped being hypothetical. BeTenshi is 31.8 GB of VRAM beside 63 GB of host RAM; B5 is a single 128 GB unified pool. Every candidate above is small enough to be unremarkable on B5 — 4.09 to 6.76 GB, all portable weights, no `runtimes` pin on any of them — so for once the fit arithmetic is not what separates the boxes. WHAT SEPARATES THEM IS WHAT WAS INSTALLED. B5 moved its speech stack to Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3-TTS on 20-09; BeTenshi added a cloning voice on 18-09 and left its transcription on a model that is open #36 of 52. So the recommendation genuinely differs by machine this week, which is the thing this section has been asking for: on BeTenshi, install Cohere Transcribe; on B5, there is nothing on this list worth doing. The older size-based asymmetries still hold and still matter for anything larger: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-7B at 17.4 GB runs alone on BeTenshi and blocks every image model, and is unremarkable on B5; Voxtral-Small-24B, inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo-FP8 at 27.58 GB, LLaDA-Image at 49.24 GB and Qwen-Image-2.1 at 33.13 GB are all refused on BeTenshi and comfortable on B5.

THE FOLLOW-ON NOBODY HAS DONE YET, unchanged and still the single cheapest win on BeTenshi: local-flux-schnell and local-qwen-image are dead weight and both are still in config/model-meta.json. Both were REJECTED by admission control during the 12 September experiment — schnell on its ~28 GB RAM / ~31.7 GB VRAM profile, Qwen-Image on its 28 GB RAM estimate against 28.94 GB available — while Z-Image-Turbo, FLUX.2-klein-4B and HiDream-O1 did the same job at 14-16 GB whole-card. Their weights are still on D: (schnell's stack alone is 31.81 GiB: flux1-schnell 22.15, t5xxl_fp16 9.12, clip_l 0.23, ae 0.31), and removing them frees more disk than every candidate on this list combined needs to download — 6.76 GB being the largest. This is a decision for a human, not a scout: schnell is the only model here anyone has A/B'd against for two years, so it should be a deliberate keep rather than an accident.

THE PATTERN WORTH REMEMBERING, and the reason this report exists beside the Leaderboard tab: for anything that is not a plain LLM, the parameter count is not the footprint, and the gap is usually a text encoder or a codec sitting outside the count. This week adds two examples and one new shape. Qwen-Image-2.1 is '7.12B' and ships 33.13 GB, because the text encoder is 17.5 GB. AuK and AuK-Flash publish NO parameter count on HF at all; the Open TTS Leaderboard records 1.53B against 6.76 GB of weights, which would be 4.4 bytes/param, so even the benchmark's figure describes a component. THE NEW SHAPE is ResembleAI/chatterbox, now installed: config/model-meta.json records 3.0 GB VRAM measured, which is right for what LOADS, but the repo is 13.87 GB on disk because it ships four separate t3 checkpoints (t3_cfg, t3_23lang, t3_mtl23ls_v2, t3_mtl23ls_v3) and both .pt and .safetensors copies of s3gen. A naive snapshot download costs 4.6x the resident footprint. That is the inverse of the usual trap and worth pricing before the next `hf download`. The back catalogue: LLaDA-Image is '6.54B' and ships 49.2 GB; FLUX.2-klein-4B is '3.88B' and ships 23.7 GB; Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B carries a 0.68 GB speech tokenizer the name omits; VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-1.5B is really 2.81B. Every requirement in this report is built from the repo's actual file byte counts, all re-read on 21-09 and all unchanged from last week.

THIS WEEK'S LEADERBOARD TRAPS, both text. Edge0/Edge0-35B-A3B-preview is still on the trending list (score 151, down from 1191, 3,550 likes), still Apache-2.0, still 19.74 GB on disk, and still `library:mlx` — Apple-silicon only, tagged `ssd-offload` and `prerouter`, a LoRA-plus-router rig over Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. It will not run on an RTX 5090 at any quantisation, however the numbers read. The new one is the opposite failure: prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf is the #1 trending text model on the entire hub this week (score 1434, 1.91M downloads in five days, apache-2.0), and its smallest build is Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf at 5,946,648,928 B — 5.95 GB for a 27B model. precisionLadderFor() bottoms out at GGUF Q2, which would price a 27B near 7-8 GB, so the console will quote a rung the repo undercuts rather than one it cannot reach. That is a conservative error rather than a dangerous one — a 27B fits BeTenshi at Q2 anyway — but the ladder has no ternary rung and should be expected to overstate anything from this family. (The #2 trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, is MIT and 763B params shipping 510 GB even at mixed fp8/int8; the Leaderboard refuses that one correctly and needs no help from this report.)

THE LIVE VENDOR LISTS WERE NOT READ THIS RUN, and the report should say so rather than imply it called them. Step 3 of docs/models.md asks for the vendor model-list endpoints, and this routine's environment has no OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY — which is correct for a cloud routine that commits to git and should not hold this box's credentials, but it means the cloud half is second-hand. What WAS verified this week came from OpenAI's public pricing page, and it is the gpt-5.5 correction recorded above. The other four upgrades rest on ids that are already wired in ai-router.yaml from the 2026-08-19 wire-all, so they are known to exist and to be reachable; none of the four was re-checked against a vendor list. The console's own discovery half calls those endpoints every 15 minutes on the machine that has the keys, which is where a current answer lives — so re-check the join in the Models page before editing an alias, exactly as the gpt-5.5 entry has been saying.

Both wired Gemini image models still report the 429 quota error recorded in model-meta.json. That is a billing state on the key, not a model choice — no scouting will fix it. Separately, gemini-pro stays pinned to gemini-3.1-pro-preview on purpose: Google publishes gemini-pro-latest as a moving alias and ai-router.yaml pins explicit versions so an archived result records which model actually produced it. Both -latest aliases are wired under their own names from the wire-all, which is fine; do not repoint a stable alias at one.

Text LLMs are deliberately absent from candidates. The Leaderboard tab ranks every open-weights text model with a published parameter count against the live card automatically, and cloud discovery carries live prices — a hand-written candidate there would go stale beside data that does not. This report's only contributions in the text lane are the gpt-5.5 upgrade above, which discovery cannot make because OpenAI's tier names look like ordinary words to familyKey(), and the two Leaderboard traps above, which are the opposite case: models the automatic ranking will size confidently and wrongly.
